Elena — thanks, this is clear. Putting a proposal together. High level first pass below; attaching a concise benchmark + cost model. Full SOW and capacity plan are in draft and I'll loop Rishi for SLA language.

Executive summary (short):
- Performance per GPU (in our workload): A100 (40GB) baseline; H100 shows ~2.0–2.4x effective throughput for generation workloads with long KV-cache utilization; L40S performs ~1.6–1.9x vs A100 depending on sequence length.
- Cost per GPU-hour (reserved pricing examples): A100: $3.00/hr; L40S: $5.00/hr; H100: $9.00/hr (note: committed discounts available).
- Perf-per-dollar (tokens/sec per $): A100 ~1500 tokens/sec/$, L40S ~2100 tokens/sec/$, H100 ~2600 tokens/sec/$ (these numbers reflect our internal kernels + quantization and the prompt distribution you shared).

Options (short):
A) Stay A100, increase pool from 8 → 18 GPUs (predictable ops; lower migration risk). Estimated monthly committed spend delta: +$9.6k.
B) Migrate entire pool to H100, commit 8 → 12 H100 (smaller headcount of GPUs required for same throughput; higher unit cost but better perf-per-dollar at scale after quant benefits). Estimated monthly committed spend delta: +$14.4k; expected 2.1x throughput vs current.
C) Mixed pool (recommended conservative path): create a 12-GPU mixed reserved pool (6 H100 + 6 L40S), migrate hottest routes to H100, persistent background inference on L40S. Estimated monthly delta: +$11.2k and better resilience.

SLA / throughput guarantees we can offer (draft):
- 99th pctl token latency SLA for provisioned routes: <250ms (for short prompts, <=256 tokens) at committed throughput.
- Committed throughput guarantee: measured as concurrent token/sec per pool; e.g., 12 H100 pool = baseline sustained 2.4M tokens/min (subject to prompt mix).

I'll attach the benchmark_summary_2026-05-14.pdf and the capacity plan. If this looks directionally right I will: (1) run a 48-hour A/B benchmark on your real prompt set, (2) finalize SOW + DocuSign links, (3) propose contract term changes (12 vs 24 mo) with step-down pricing.

—Priyom

Tom — good questions. Short answers and specifics below. Detailed numbers are in the attached capacity_plan and SOW draft.

1) Discount breakpoints (example):
- H100 base: $9.00/hr. Committed discounts apply at 24 GPU-months (≈10% → $8.10/hr) and 48 GPU-months (≈22% → $7.00/hr). We can show a modeled pricing ladder in the SOW.

2) Mixed pool billing: we bill by GPU-class hours. You receive line-item usage for H100 and L40S; committed discounts apply per class. For commitment accounting we roll up to a single monthly committed spend target (you can designate which class counts toward commitment on a monthly basis).

Fallback options (automated routing policies):
- Primary: route to same-class reserved pool (H100) if capacity exists.
- Secondary fallback: route to compatible L40S variant with automatic quantization profile (expected median latency +12–20% vs H100; perf-per-dollar still favorable).
- Tertiary: scale to on-demand A100 in other regions (higher latency/cost) — used only if pool and cross-region failover required.

Operational plan (recommended):
Phase 0 (pre-renewal): 48-hour A/B benchmark on your production prompt sample (we'll do this in your tenant).
Phase 1: Deploy mixed pool (6 H100 + 6 L40S) and migrate 20% of traffic to H100 as canary (2 weeks).
Phase 2: If canary meets latency and quality gates, increase H100 routing to 60% over 2 weeks.
Phase 3: Finalize committed counts and sign SOW. Rolling fallback and tracing configured via Redwood Console.

I'll have Marissa and Rishi add SLA language and Ops runbook.

—Priyom

Looping in operations / SLA specifics. A few clarifications we add to SOW draft:
- Measurement: committed throughput defined as sustained token/sec over 10-minute windows, measured at ingress gateway. Burst allowance: 15% above commitment for up to 5 consecutive minutes.
- Credits: SLA credits for sustained violation (>10 minutes) of committed throughput or 99th pctl latency. Credit formula in SOW (percentage of monthly committed spend).
- Maintenance windows: scheduled monthly maintenance windows will be notified 7 days in advance; emergency maintenance with minimal notice only in critical cases and with make-good credits.

Operational note: for quantization-sensitive models (your re-ranker), we recommend H100 for early inference (low latency, long KV cache). L40S works well for batched bulk embedding or lower-variance generation.

I'll attach SOW_draft_SKY_H100_migration.docx and a short runbook.

—Rishi Malhotra
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
